source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide why rocks, soil, minerals, and geodiversity are life-supporting rather than lifeless background.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Earth's crust is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Soil nutrients come from the slow breakdown of rocks and remains of plants and animals.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: nutrient-rich soils and habitats -> plant growth and survival of living things happens first, and that produces rock breakdown, organic remains, and varied landforms.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Soil nutrients come from the slow breakdown of rocks and remains of plants and animals is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth's crust, made of rocks, soil, and minerals, provides materials life needs; soil contains nutrients such as nitrogen and potassium, and geodiversity creates varied habitats for different living things. rock breakdown, organic remains, and varied landforms -> nutrient-rich soils and habitats -> plant growth and survival of living things The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Earth's crust, made of rocks, soil, and minerals, provides materials life needs; soil contains nutrients such as nitrogen and potassium, and geodiversity creates varied habitats for different living things. Rocks and minerals are non-living, so they cannot help living things survive.
